Its related to uncommenting and enabling `pad_argument_buffer_resources = true`

Is this an exported project? Given you mentioned lazy, I suspect you are, as that the default on iOS devices. 

I'm quite certain that the issue will be baking shaders, based on the following:

- The Godot export process is using your Mac's device profile which will report true for `SUPPORTS_IMAGE_ATOMIC_32_BIT`
  
  https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ac8202c60a58b7e4bddef9aada8cc259e05ec0f8/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/environment/fog.cpp#L52
- The export process therefore passes a shader with image atomics to be baked
- The export is dependent on your target OS version, which quite possible will be 2.4 MSL shader version (or 3.0). These versions of MSL do not support native image atomics, and therefore SPIR-V Cross falls back to trying to emulate image atomics (not supported)
- Crash

As a test, can you override the minimum OS version so that it is iOS 17 and macOS 14, both of which support Metal 3.1, which is required for Image Atomics.

This might be a bit more complicated to address, as we'd have to influence the backing process to generate a compatible shader.

For the crash, yes this is an exported project and the metal version I run is 3.2. The reason for the lazy flag is that a 3+ minute start time is not acceptable for a commercial game. Shader baker is on, but the PSO (?) compilation times are not ideal. 

For the white screen, that happens regardless of of the project being exported or not. I did a temporary fix (because the PR that introduces atomics should handle the secondary binding / index that causes the crash).

> For the crash, yes this is an exported project and the metal version I run is 3.2.

Are you overriding the target OS version when exporting? If not, you'll be using the default OS target, which is a lower version of Metal (I think 2.4). The shader baker process will specifically bake for that target OS's version of Metal, despite your device starting with Metal 3.2. Given you are building on an M3 and macOS 15, the Fog shader will think you want image atomics, but the target Metal version does not support it. That will generate _incorrect_ shader code, based on the current Shader Baker architecture, which still has a few cases where it relies on your host machine's feature set.

It is compounded with lazy, is the pipeline isn't compiled until it is first used by the renderer, rather than at shader compilation time in Godot. If the shader fails at compilation time, Godot will regenerate the shader which would resolve the error for your target device.

Interesting. I will check and try this in about 10h. I still feel there is a fix lurking here, such as having the shader baker compile for more targets or using some sort of metal based cache key during runtime.

Before this I ran my clear cache shaders script, hopefully it is correct:

```
echo "========================================"
echo "     Shader Cache Cleaner for macOS"
echo "========================================"
echo ""

# Find project.godot - check current directory first, then parent
PROJECT_FILE="project.godot"
if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_FILE" ]; then
    if [ -f "../project.godot" ]; then
        echo "Found project.godot in parent directory, switching to project root..."
        cd ..
        PROJECT_FILE="project.godot"
    else
        echo "ERROR: Could not find project.godot in current or parent directory"
        echo "Make sure to run this script from your project root or tools folder"
        echo "Usage: ./tools/clear_shader_cache.sh"
        exit 1
    fi
fi

# Get project name from project.godot
PROJECT_NAME=$(grep "config/name" "$PROJECT_FILE" | cut -d'=' -f2 | tr -d '"' | tr -d ' ')

if [ -z "$PROJECT_NAME" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Could not parse project name from project.godot"
    exit 1
fi

echo "Project detected: $PROJECT_NAME"
echo ""
echo "This will clear all compiled shaders for this project."
echo "Press Ctrl+C to cancel, or Enter to continue..."
read

# Check if Godot is running
if pgrep -x "Godot" > /dev/null; then
    echo "WARNING: Godot appears to be running. Please quit it first!"
    echo "Press Enter to exit..."
    read
    exit 1
fi

echo ""
echo "Clearing shader caches..."

# Clear global Godot shader cache (engine shaders like VolumetricFog)
echo "- Removing global Godot shader cache..."
rm -rf ~/Library/Application\ Support/Godot/shader_cache/ 2>/dev/null

# Clear user data shader caches
echo "- Removing user shader cache..."
rm -rf ~/Library/Application\ Support/Godot/app_userdata/"$PROJECT_NAME"/shader_cache/ 2>/dev/null
rm -rf ~/Library/Application\ Support/Godot/app_userdata/"$PROJECT_NAME"/vulkan/ 2>/dev/null

# Clear project-local cache
echo "- Removing project shader cache..."
rm -rf .godot/shader_cache/ 2>/dev/null

# Clear GPU driver cache
echo "- Clearing GPU driver caches..."
rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/com.apple.metal/ 2>/dev/null
rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/GPUCache/ 2>/dev/null


# Clear app-specific Metal shader cache in /var/folders
# This is where Metal stores compiled shaders per bundle ID
BUNDLE_ID=$(grep "macos/bundle_identifier" "$PROJECT_FILE" 2>/dev/null | cut -d'=' -f2 | tr -d '"' | tr -d ' ')
if [ -z "$BUNDLE_ID" ]; then
    # Fallback to common pattern if not found in project.godot
    BUNDLE_ID="gg.talonbyte.kindling"
fi
USER_CACHE_DIR=$(getconf DARWIN_USER_CACHE_DIR)
if [ -d "${USER_CACHE_DIR}${BUNDLE_ID}" ]; then
    echo "- Clearing Metal shader cache for $BUNDLE_ID..."
    rm -rf "${USER_CACHE_DIR}${BUNDLE_ID}" 2>/dev/null
fi

echo ""
echo "========================================"
echo "           Cache cleared!"
echo "   Next Godot launch will recompile"
echo "         all shaders (20-60 sec)"
echo "========================================"
echo ""
echo "Press Enter to exit..."*
```

@stuartcarnie After a bit back and fourth it no longer crashes, with 14.0 (not 14.00, but that might be irrelevant). I now have trouble getting back into the crashing state but the entire screen is white so something fishy is going on. My fog shader depends on two textures: - Height (it follows terrain) - Density (there are cleared paths through the fog) After I did set these two textures to something, in my warmup scene, then it started to work. Unclear if that is related and that the shader baker was doing something interesting without it set before (different variants?). It might also have been a fluke. That said, now the crash is gone, but the entire scene is white (not the 2d elements) and the last time this happened was on 4.5.1 with SSIL enabled which for unknown reasons pushed `nan` into the color channels which was then interpreted as "all white" (on D3D12, Windows). Disabling SSIL fixed to problem but I went back to Vulkan regardless. This is the first time I see it on macOS. Running xcodes metal debugger shows that there is a step that turns the entire screen white. Its something about blur_1 into what might be the tone mapper. Also, attaching the Xcode metal debugger to it shows a bunch of warnings, but maybe that is normal:
